nodes.node_name: 📝 Prompt Ảnh 1: Khu Đất & Móng Công Trình
nodes.prompt:
Using the completed building reference, recreate the exact same location after the previous building has been completely demolished.

Keep the camera absolutely identical.

Preserve without any change:

neighboring buildings
street
sidewalks
road markings
utility poles
power cables
sky
ambient lighting
perspective
framing
composition

Remove the entire building only.

Replace it with a clean rectangular vacant construction lot.

Visible details:

compacted dirt
light gravel
construction boundary markers
temporary wooden stakes
simple construction fence at the back
slight excavation marks
no vegetation

The empty lot should occupy exactly the same footprint as the future building.

Everything surrounding the lot remains unchanged.

Photorealistic architectural photography.

nodes.node_name: 📝 Prompt Ảnh 2: Thi Công Khung Thép & Cẩu
nodes.prompt:
Completed Foundation

Use the supplied completed building image as the architectural and environment reference.

Recreate the exact same location, camera angle, perspective, framing, composition, focal length, neighboring buildings, sidewalks, street, utility poles, overhead cables, lighting, sky color and all surrounding environmental details.

The camera is perfectly locked.

The future building footprint remains identical to the reference building.

Show the construction site immediately after the foundation has been completed.

Visible construction details include:

• completed reinforced concrete foundation
• concrete footing system
• foundation beams
• reinforced concrete slab
• anchor bolts
• foundation starter columns protruding upward
• underground utility pipes partially visible
• compacted construction soil surrounding the foundation
• stacks of reinforcing steel
• wooden formwork removed and stacked nearby
• several construction materials neatly arranged
• a small excavator parked nearby
• realistic construction workers wearing safety helmets
• temporary safety fencing around the site

No walls.

No structural floors.

No stair core.

No windows.

No doors.

No scaffolding.

No architectural elements above foundation level except short starter columns.

Everything outside the construction footprint remains identical to the supplied reference image.

Ultra photorealistic architectural photography.

Natural evening lighting identical to the reference.

Highly detailed concrete texture.

Physically accurate Japanese urban construction site.

nodes.node_name: 📝 Prompt Ảnh 3: Hoàn Thiện Mặt Kính & Ánh Sáng
nodes.prompt:
Use Frame 2, the finished-building image, as the sole source image and absolute architectural blueprint.

Create an unfinished pre-glazing construction version of exactly the same building by removing only installed finish elements. This is a precise image-editing task, not a redesign and not a generic structural-shell generation.

Preserve the finished building’s architecture exactly and pixel-consistently:

identical building width and height
identical exterior silhouette
identical roofline
identical wall geometry
identical concrete facade
identical concrete panel seams
identical circular form-tie holes
identical ground-floor slanted columns
identical ground-floor recessed storefront opening
identical upper-floor recessed opening
identical upper-floor window divisions
identical solid concrete middle facade
identical camera position, lens, framing and perspective
identical neighboring buildings, utility pole, overhead cables, road and pavement

Critical architecture rule:

The middle concrete facade must remain completely solid and uninterrupted exactly as shown in Frame 2.

Do not create any middle-floor window.

Do not create any additional opening in the concrete facade.

At the upper floor, preserve the exact two window openings and their exact dimensions from Frame 2. Remove only the glass and finished aluminum window components, leaving the same openings empty or partially prepared for installation.

At the ground floor, preserve the exact completed storefront opening, slanted concrete columns, upper beam, recessed depth, entrance position and glass-panel divisions from Frame 2. Remove only the storefront glass, door and finished frames.

The concrete structure must already be identical to the final building. No structural construction remains.

Show the building immediately before glazing installation:

empty upper window openings matching Frame 2
empty ground-floor storefront opening matching Frame 2
mounting brackets and unfinished frame channels inside the openings
temporary safety rails located only inside open areas
light scaffolding positioned in front of the facade
several workers preparing the openings
neatly stacked window frames and glass panels on the ground
limited construction tools and materials
unfinished interior visible through the openings
no furniture
no decorative lighting
no potted plants

Do not add concrete where glass belongs.

Do not remove concrete where the final building has concrete.

Do not alter the facade to make it look more like a conventional construction shell.

Do not invent windows, balconies, columns, walls or openings.

The generated image must align with Frame 2 when overlaid. The only differences should be glazing, doors, interior finishing, furniture, lighting, plants, workers, scaffolding and construction materials.

Photorealistic fixed-camera architectural construction photography.

nodes.prompt:
FINAL VIDEO PROMPT
(Frame Start → Frame End)

Frame Start is the absolute architectural truth.

Frame End is the same building after construction finishing.

This is NOT an architectural generation task.

This is NOT a building redesign task.

This is NOT a building reconstruction task.

This is an architectural finishing edit.

The reinforced-concrete building shown in Frame Start already exists exactly as intended.

Treat the entire building in Frame Start as a permanently frozen architectural object.

Never regenerate the building.

Never reinterpret the building.

Never redesign the building.

Never improve the building.

Never optimize the building.

Never reconstruct the building.

Never replace the architecture.

Never generate an alternative facade.

Never infer missing architectural details.

Never invent a more realistic building.

Never create a more conventional facade.

Never create a more symmetrical facade.

Never create a more modern facade.

Never generate architecture from scratch.

The concrete building itself is completely immutable.

Everything made of reinforced concrete is permanently read-only.

Read-only objects include:

• front concrete facade

• left concrete wall

• right concrete wall

• roof slab

• recessed roof opening

• upper recessed balcony volume

• entire middle concrete wall

• ground floor concrete frame

• slanted concrete side columns

• concrete beams

• concrete slabs

• concrete corners

• concrete edges

• concrete thickness

• concrete panel layout

• construction joints

• circular form-tie holes

• every existing opening boundary

• every existing wall boundary

None of these objects may ever:

move

shift

resize

rotate

bend

warp

stretch

collapse

split

merge

morph

transform

be regenerated

be redesigned

be replaced

be removed

be extended

be shortened

become glass

become windows

become doors

become curtain walls

be covered by new concrete

be covered by new glazing

The architectural geometry visible in Frame Start must remain visually identical during the entire video.

If any architectural conflict exists between Frame Start and Frame End,

Frame Start is always correct.

Never create transitional architecture.

Never invent intermediate architecture.

Never generate temporary facade designs.

Never create temporary windows.

Never create temporary openings.

Never create temporary curtain walls.

The only editable regions are:

• upper left window opening

• upper right window opening

• ground-floor storefront opening

These openings already exist in Frame Start.

Do not resize them.

Do not move them.

Do not reshape them.

Do not subdivide them.

Do not merge them.

Do not create additional openings.

The middle concrete wall is permanently outside the editable region.

No worker touches this wall.

No installation occurs there.

No scaffold modifies it.

No drilling occurs there.

No cutting occurs there.

No window may ever appear there.

No glass may ever appear there.

No opening may ever appear there.

Only the following objects are allowed to change:

temporary scaffolding

temporary safety rails

construction workers

construction tools

construction materials

glass panels

aluminum window frames

storefront glazing

entrance doors

temporary work lights

interior finishing

floor finishing

ceiling finishing

electrical fixtures

interior furniture

decorative plants

final cleaning

Construction sequence:

Workers prepare the existing openings.

Aluminum window frames are carried into the existing openings.

Frames are mechanically fixed into place.

Glass panels are lifted and installed inside those exact frames.

Ground-floor storefront glazing is installed.

Entrance doors are installed.

Interior finishing progresses naturally behind the glass.

Furniture is carried through the entrance and arranged inside.

Decorative plants are placed.

Temporary construction materials are removed.

Scaffolding is dismantled.

Workers leave.

The entrance and pavement are cleaned.

Interior lighting gradually turns on.

Throughout the entire sequence,

the reinforced-concrete architecture never changes.

No structural construction occurs.

No concrete work occurs.

No facade reconstruction occurs.

No architectural redesign occurs.

Frame End is only the confirmation that finishing work has been completed on the immutable building from Frame Start.

Do not transform the building toward Frame End.

Instead, preserve the building from Frame Start and only complete the remaining finishing work until the final appearance naturally matches Frame End.
